subject: angol
title: Money, spending and saving
instructionsHu: A vizsgáztató a pénzkezelési szokásaidról, a vásárlásról, a reklámokról és a pénzügyi tudatosságról kérdez. Válaszolj részletesen, indokold a véleményedet, és mondj példákat.

questions.q: How do you usually manage your money? Do you keep track of what you spend?
Should teenagers get pocket money, or should they earn their own money? Why?
What is the best thing you have ever spent money on? Why?
followUps: Have you ever regretted buying something?

questions.q: How do advertisements influence what you buy?
Do you think young people today are more materialistic than their parents' generation?
What are the risks of shopping online or buying things on credit?
followUps: Do you know anyone who has had a bad experience?

questions.q: Should financial education be taught at school? What should it include?
Do you think money can buy happiness? Why or why not?
What is the biggest financial challenge for young people starting out in life?
If you won a large amount of money, how would you use it?

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: How do you usually manage your money? Do you keep track of what you spend?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I get a fixed amount of pocket money every month, and I earn a bit extra by tutoring a younger neighbour in maths. I keep track of everything in a budgeting app, and it's quite shocking how much I spend on snacks.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Should teenagers get pocket money, or should they earn their own money? Why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Ideally, both. Pocket money teaches you to plan ahead, but earning your own money, even with a summer job, makes you realise how much work goes into every thousand forints.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: What is the best thing you have ever spent money on? Why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Probably a second-hand bike. I'd saved up for it for months, and now I cycle to school every day instead of buying a bus pass, so it has more or less paid for itself.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Have you ever regretted buying something?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Oh, definitely. I once bought really expensive trainers just because everyone in my class had them, and I hardly ever wore them. Since then, I've always waited a week before buying anything big.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Do you think money can buy happiness? Why or why not?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Up to a point, yes. If you're constantly worried about paying the bills, it's very hard to be happy. But beyond a certain level, I'd say experiences and relationships count for far more than possessions.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: minden válasz kifejtett és személyes (korrepetálás, használt bicikli, a megbánt drága edzőcipő), az elvont kérdésre – boldogság és pénz – pedig árnyalt, két oldalt mérlegelő választ ad.

Nyelvhelyesség: B2-es igeidők pontosan – Past Perfect (I'd saved up for it), Present Perfect (it has more or less paid for itself; Since then, I've always waited) –, valamint feltételes mellékmondat és a 'make you realise' szerkezet.
Szókincs: a pénzügyek pontos szavai (pocket money, budgeting app, bus pass, possessions) és jól használt árnyaló fordulatok (Ideally, Up to a point, I'd say).
Érdemes megtanulni: „keep track of everything”, „it has more or less paid for itself”, „Up to a point, yes”, „count for far more than”.
